title: Rollback Triage Timeline with Incident Annotations Prototype
creator: Morgan Reyes
description:
Problem statement: When a rollout degrades, engineers and PMs need a fast, contextual way in the Console to decide whether to rollback. Current consoles show metrics and logs in separate panels; teams spend precious minutes correlating exposure, error spikes, and configuration changes. This design explores a compact, annotated timeline that overlays rollout exposure with incident signals and curated annotations to accelerate triage and safe rollback decisions.

Goals:
- Surface temporal correlations between traffic shifts and signal anomalies (errors, latency, quality regressions) in a single view.
- Provide audited incident annotations (linked to PagerDuty/incidents) and automated anomaly snippets from the observability pipeline.
- Offer a lightweight, safe rollback composer: prefilled reason templates, impact estimate (users affected, percent), and rollback scope (variant, region, percent).
- Make the flow accessible and keyboard-first for on-call use.

Key UX elements explored in the prototype:
1) Exposure track: compact area chart showing rollout percentage over time, with minute-level granularity on hover.
2) Signal lanes: stacked annotations for errors, latency, QA regression scores, and custom telemetry events. Each annotation includes source (metrics, evals, user reports) and confidence score.
3) Incident anchors: tappable markers that expand into a contextual panel with incident summary, link to incident timeline, and suggested correlation highlights (e.g., same timestamp as spike in 95th p99 latency).
4) Snapshot compare: take two timestamps from the timeline and show a side-by-side delta of key metrics and recent model responses (sampled) to help reason about quality regressions.
5) Quick rollback composer: a modal reachable from timeline that auto-fills a rollback rationale based on selected annotations, shows expected scope & cost delta, and provides a preflight checklist (runbook link, required approvals).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Compact vs. detailed: we prioritize speed for on-call; drill-downs take users to full metric dashboards rather than clutter the timeline.
- Automation surface: provide suggested correlations but never auto-rollback — keep control with human-in-the-loop approvals.
- Privacy: sampled model responses are redacted by default; users can opt into additional context.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype enables a user to identify a correlated incident and begin a rollback with <= 3 clicks from a rollout detail page.
- Timeline annotations show relevant incident links and at least one automated correlation suggestion in 90% of internal test cases.
- Quick rollback composer populates reason text and estimated affected percent based on timeline selection and shows a cost delta estimate within +/- 15%.
- Keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels implemented for timeline marks and composer controls.

Constraints / notes for engineering:
- Needs ingestion of structured incident metadata from the incident system and a lightweight anomaly feed (ENG-550900).
- Snapshot compare requires a short-term sample store (30–60 minutes) or integration with existing query APIs.
- Visual performance: timeline must remain responsive at 1s resolution for up to 2 hours of data; consider downsampling and progressive loading.
